subject: MeridianDB pilot: S3 + pgvector fallthrough pilot and residency questions
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@meridiandb.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example>
Cc: MeridianDB Partnerships <partners@meridiandb.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro — pilot partnership (S3 + pgvector fallthrough)

Hi Avery —

Thanks for the quick intro at SCALE last week. MeridianDB is interested in piloting a hybrid index flow where heavy cold storage lives in S3 and active vectors live in pgvector (we run managed pgvector clusters). Our success criteria are:

- <48ms tail lookup for top-K over active set (warm)
- Deterministic fallthrough to S3 for cold results without impacting p99 latency beyond SLAs
- Clear data residency controls for EU customers (we have an EU tenant requirement)

Attached is a short POC requirements sheet that lays out the test vectors and workload shapes. High-level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood surface a predictable routing policy so we can replicate how queries fall through?
- What controls exist to pin model and vector-store combinations for customers?
- Can you share SOC2 evidence and retention/audit logs for embeddings?

If convenient I’d like to propose a 6-week pilot: week 0 intake + infra; weeks 1–3 functional tests and latency bench; weeks 4–5 production traffic shadow; week 6 wrap + results.

Would next Tue/Wed work for a kickoff?

Cheers,
Samir
Head of Partnerships — MeridianDB
attachments: MeridianDB-POC-Requirements.pdf
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example>
To: Samir Patel <samir@meridiandb.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — pilot partnership (S3 + pgvector fallthrough)

Hi Samir —

Really glad to connect. MeridianDB’s POC brief looks clear — thanks for sending it over. We’re excited about partnering on a hybrid index flow; that’s exactly the kind of interoperability customers ask for.

Quick answers up front:
- Routing policy: yes — Redwood can apply a route-by-policy that pins queries to region/model/vector-store combos. We also support automatic fallback to a configured cold-store path (S3) with a configurable timeout window so warm-path latency is preserved.
- Pinning controls + rollouts: supported via per-account model pins + rollout policies (canary/A-B) in the Console; we’ll share a short demo during kickoff.
- SOC2 + logs: see Samir — we can provide our SOC2 summary and audit-log export format. I’ll attach our SOC2 summary and a template for audit log ingestion.

Proposed kickoff times: Wed May 1 10:00am PT or Thu May 2 2:00pm PT — which is better for you?

Pilot scope (proposed minimal viable test):
1) Intake: network peering options (VPC or cross-account IAM), region mapping for EU tenants, baseline dataset transfer (we’ll do a 1TB sample snapshot to an S3 bucket).
2) Functional: route to pgvector for top-50k vectors; simulate fallthrough path to S3 for >90th percentile cold queries.
3) Latency/Cost: run mixed QPS profile (200QPS peak, 25 sustained) and capture token/embedding unit costs.
4) Ops: exercise KV cache invalidation and reindex flow; verify logs exported to Meridian’s SIEM.

I’m looping in Laura for legal/commercial and Ben to scope resource commitments (GPU pool + infra). Vanessa — can you confirm whether we can offer a 90-day evaluation rate for committed engineering support for this pilot?

Samir — attached is a short intake checklist and our SOC2 summary.

Thanks,
Avery
Sr. Partner Sales — Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood-intake-checklist.pdf; Redwood-SOC2-summary.txt
From: Samir Patel <samir@meridiandb.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example>
Cc: MeridianDB Partnerships <partners@meridiandb.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — pilot partnership (S3 + pgvector fallthrough)

Avery / Laura / Ben —

Appreciate the rapid reply and clarity. Wed May 1 10:00am PT works for our onboarding lead (Claire) and me. We have a few clarifications before kickoff so the kickoff agenda is actionable:

Technical clarifications:
- Cold fallthrough: when Redwood hits the timeout and routes to S3, does the system stream partial results back to the caller or buffer until full result available? We prefer streaming for large result sets.
- auth: for S3 read access, can we use an IAM role that Redwood assumes per-customer, or do you require long-lived keys?
- metrics: what traces/metrics do you export for cross-correlation (e.g., request id mapping to cache hit/miss, vector-store hit boolean, reroute reason)?

Commercial / compliance asks:
- We need to confirm retention of embedding vectors in both warm and cold tiers — is there an admin-facing retention policy and ability to run delete-by-customer-id?
- SOC2: thanks, please send the summary and the format for audit-log exports.

I’ve attached the POC requirements and a short Meridian runbook that describes our pgvector cluster sizing.

See you Wed — Claire will join from our Cloud Ops team.

Best,
Samir
attachments: MeridianDB-runbook-pgvector-sizing.pdf; MeridianDB-POC-Requirements.pdf
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir@meridiandb.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Intro — pilot partnership (S3 + pgvector fallthrough) — internal next steps

Ben / Vanessa / Laura — forwarding the Meridian thread. Key asks to resolve before Wed kickoff:

1) Streaming fallthrough: Meridian prefers streaming partial results when S3 reads are large. Engineering: what’s the implementation effort to support chunked fallthrough streaming vs buffering? (Estimate in dev-weeks; include test/observability work).
2) IAM role assumption for S3: product/legal — can we document a short flow where customers provide a cross-account role that Redwood assumes? Any blocking compliance flags for enterprise MSA?
3) Audit/export contract: Laura — they want an admin-facing retention policy + delete-by-customer-id. Can we commit to that in a pilot? If not, propose an interim workaround (time-limited export + manual deletes).
4) Pilot discount / evaluation rate: Vanessa — can we offer up to 90 days of dedicated engineering support at a discounted rate (proposed 50% engineering time billed to Meridian) and a pilot credit for Hosted token usage?

I’ve attached the draft MSA redlines we typically use for partner pilots — use as a starting point. I’ll be on the kickoff Wed 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Avery
Sr. Partner Sales — Redwood Inference
